summary: Comprehensively reframe the LRC(14) coverage/lonely-measure bound as inclusion-exclusion over a natural number N (3=cube-root/C3, 6=Z2xZ3, 7=sectors/apex, runners), each angle developed concretely, then synthesize the most promising proof route

findings.reframing: REFRAMING A (cube-root C_3 inclusion–exclusion). Multiplication by 2 mod 7 partitions the 7 sectors into three C_3 orbits: {0}, A={1,2,4} (=QR), B={3,5,6} (=NQR). Reindex the coverage sieve p0(E)=sum_{S subset {0..6}}(-1)^|S| m_S(E) not over the 2^7=128 subsets S but over the C_3-orbit TYPE of S, the triple t(S)=(1_{0 in S}, |S∩A|, |S∩B|). This collapses 128 subsets to 32 types. The proposed identity is a "C_3 trace": replace m_S by its dilation average m_S^avg = (1/3)(m_S + m_{2S} + m_{4S}) and sum the sieve over types, p0 = sum_{types t} N(t)(-1)^{|t|} m^avg(t), where N(t)=C(3,|A|)C(3,|B|). On the main term M7(k)=sum_T(-1)^|T|(1-|T|/7)^{k-1} this is EXACT and trivial (M7 depends only on |T|, so the (|A|,|B|) refinement reproduces it identically — verified k=7..14). The substantive part is the correction p0-M7, where C_3 acts nontrivially.
findings.whatItBuys: Concretely it isolates the genuinely-arithmetic part of the correction into a SMALL residual. After C_3-averaging on the canonical symmetric cluster E={0..6}: 28 of the 32 orbit-types collapse to a single m^avg value (so those 28 are determined by the closed-form decorrelated kernel and contribute a rational, C_3-symmetric block). Only 4 types survive: (s0,|A|,|B|) = (0,1,1),(0,1,2),(0,2,1),(0,2,2) — exactly the CROSS-ORBIT types where S meets BOTH A and B. These 4 carry all the residual correlation. So the reframing manifests the cancellation of the 28 "pure/diagonal" orbit-types and isolates the 4 cross-orbit (QR×NQR) coupling terms as the only obstruction. It does NOT bound p0 or L(S) by itself; it reduces the unknown part of the correction from O(2^k) subset terms to 4 cross-orbit type-classes. The Z/2 (QR↔NQR, mult by 3 = the n↔-n / HYP-2657 reality) swaps A and B and pairs (0,1,2)<->(0,2,1), (0,1,1) and (0,2,2) self-paired — so the real correction is governed by 3 independent cross-orbit numbers.

(5) DECISIVE: 128 subsets -> 32 (s0,|A|,|B|) types; raw, only 20/32 collapse; after C_3-averaging 28/32 collapse exactly, residual = exactly the 4 cross-orbit types listed, with values e.g. type(0,1,1)={0.1175,0.1349,0.1476}. Main term M7 C_3-coarsened == M7 verified k=7..14.
findings.proofRoute: The reframing does NOT give a new bound directly; the route it suggests is narrow but concrete: prove the 4 cross-orbit residual types are individually bounded (or sign-controlled) by an order-3 QR×NQR coupling estimate. The needed lemma: for the covering cluster E, the cross-orbit correction C_AB(E) = sum over the 3 inequivalent cross-orbit type-classes of (-1)^|S| (m_S - m^avg) is bounded by the two-far apex constant 13/(2^2·7^3) (the documented two-far curvature). Since these are precisely the |T|=2 "mixed" relation-lattice terms, this connects to the OPEN signed-magnitude bound for d>=2: the C_3 split says you only need the bound for QR×NQR mixed pairs, not all C(6,2) pairs — a factor-of-2 reduction (3 classes instead of 6 unordered pairs) plus the reality (HYP-2657) from -1 being NQR. Combined with the Galois-equivariance D7(ac)=σ_a(D7(c)), the diagonal (pure-A, pure-B) blocks rationalize completely. Caveat: this is a reorganization of the existing d>=2 obstruction, not a resolution; the cross-orbit coupling is exactly where the absolute-bound is 5x lossy, so the hard analytic content remains.

findings.reframing:
REFRAMING B (N=6 via (Z/7)*=Z/2 x Z/3 characters). Setup: 0 in E always hits sector 0, so the live object is the 6 nonzero sectors {1..6}. The coverage sieve is p0(E)=sum_{S subset {0..6}}(-1)^|S| m_S(E), m_S=meas{tau: orbit {frac(e tau)} misses every sector in S}. The dilation group (Z/7)* acts on integer clusters by E -> a*E and on sectors by j -> a*j mod 7. Decompose over the 6 characters of (Z/7)*: chi_0 (trivial), chi_3 (sign = QR/NQR, order 2), chi_2,chi_4 (cube-root, order 3 = the C_3), chi_1,chi_5 (order 6). 

The decomposition is applied at TWO levels and they behave oppositely:
(1) On p0 ITSELF: p0(a*E)=p0(E) EXACTLY for all a in (Z/7)* (integer dilation invariance, verified exact on random and structured E). Hence for any nontrivial chi_k, sum_a chi_k(a) p0(aE) = p0(E)*sum_a chi_k(a) = 0. So p0 carries 100% of its multiplicative-character mass in chi_0; the sign, cube-root, and order-6 pieces VANISH identically. The coverage is a pure trivial-character object under dilation.
(2) On the SECTOR-RESOLVED miss masses m_S: dilation acts on the 2^6 subsets of {1..6}, giving exactly 14 orbits. The character mass lives here. The key carriers: the size-2 orbit {{1,2,4},{3,5,6}} is EXACTLY the cube-roots-of-unity coset {1,2,4}=QR and its complement {3,5,6}=NQR. m_QR=m_{124} and m_NQR=m_{356}; their SUM is the chi_0 piece, their DIFFERENCE m_QR-m_NQR is the sign-character (chi_3) Gauss-sum mass. The order-3 (cube-root) characters chi_2,chi_4 split WITHIN the QR triple {1,2,4} via 1+omega*2+omega^2*4. The antipodal pairs {1,6},{2,5},{3,4} (the size-3 orbit of {j,-j}) are the n<->-n reality carriers in the 2-far layer.

Crucially: the single-sector miss vector q_j=m_{{j}} is symmetric under the ADDITIVE reflection j->6-j (from the geometric involution tau->1-tau, which maps sector j to 6-j and is measure-preserving), but is NOT symmetric under multiplicative inversion j->-j mod 7. So q is an additive object; the multiplicative C_3/sign structure only appears cleanly on the dilation-orbit-grouped subset masses, not on the raw sector vector.
findings.whatItBuys: It cleanly SEPARATES the two symmetry types that the canon had conflated. (a) It isolates the cube-root C_3 piece as a single concrete scalar: the imbalance within m_{124} (QR = cube roots of unity mod 7) under 1+omega*m_2+omega^2*m_4, which is bounded and explicitly Eisenstein (lives in Z[omega]). (b) It reproduces the known n<->-n reality as the chi_3 sign character: the difference m_QR-m_NQR = m_{124}-m_{356}, exactly the Gauss-sum splitting of QR vs NQR. (c) It PROVES (not just observes) that the coverage p0 has zero nontrivial multiplicative-character content -- this is the rigorous version of the canon note that 'the full F_7^* trace collapse needs equal archimedean weights and fails': the collapse holds perfectly on the mod-7 reduced (dilation) action because p0 is exactly dilation-invariant, but p0 does NOT depend only on residues mod 7 (verified: two clusters with identical profile (1,2,2,2,1,0,0) give p0=0.094048 vs 0.095130), so the archimedean integer-spacing dependence is the genuine obstruction to a pure-character bound. This tells the proof exactly which term it can bound by characters (the dilation-invariant chi_0 main mass = M7) and which residual (the archimedean leak inside chi_0) must be handled by Poisson/theta keeping (-1)^|T|.

findings.proofRoute: The reframing tells the proof to STOP trying to bound the correction by multiplicative characters of p0 (provably zero there) and instead attack the archimedean leak inside chi_0. Concrete next lemma: bound |p0(E) - p0_residue(E)| where p0_residue is the dilation-AND-residue-invariant approximation, by a theta/Poisson estimate over the integer spacings, keeping the (-1)^|S| sign and the 7-vanishing of the main term M7. Specifically: (i) prove m_QR-m_NQR (the chi_3 sign Gauss-sum mass) is bounded by c/k^2 type decay (the data 0.004082, 0.007653 suggests it shrinks with E spread but grows for tight cube-root-orbit clusters -- needs a clean upper bound); (ii) show the cube-root chi_2 piece, being valued in Z[omega] with norm a^2-ab+b^2, contributes a strictly bounded Eisenstein term that can be absorbed; (iii) combine with the proven chi_0=M7 main term (TINY, ~0.0245 at k=8) to get p0 <= M7 + bounded-char-residual, then check this against cap_8=2243/5880=0.3815. The honest gap: this still requires the archimedean residual bound, the SAME open d>=2 signed-magnitude bound noted in the state of proof -- the character reframing localizes it but does not yet close it.

findings.reframing:
REFRAMING C (coverage sieve over N=7 sectors + Bonferroni/Brun truncation). Natural number N=7 (the sectors). Let A_j = {x in [0,1): no e in E sends frac(e*x) into sector j} = "sector j is never hit by the orbit." Then {x: orbit hits ALL 7 sectors} = complement of union_j A_j, so

  p0(E) = 1 - meas(union_{j=0}^6 A_j) = sum_{S subset {0..6}} (-1)^|S| m_S(E),  m_S = meas(intersect_{j in S} A_j) = meas{x: every sector in S is missed}, m_empty=1.

INCLUDED/EXCLUDED: we sieve out the configurations that miss at least one sector. m_S is the measure of x missing every sector in S. Bonferroni cumulative partial sums give ALTERNATING bounds. With U = meas(union A_j) = sum_k (-1)^{k+1} Sigma_k, Sigma_k = sum_{|S|=k} m_S, the truncations give p0 >= 1-Sigma_1, p0 <= 1-Sigma_1+Sigma_2, p0 >= 1-Sigma_1+Sigma_2-Sigma_3, ... So EVEN cumulative levels are UPPER bounds on p0 (the side we want for p0<=cap), ODD are LOWER.

TWO EXACT VANISHING FACTS that shape the sieve: (1) Because 0 in E (the co-offset cluster always contains 0), sector 0 is ALWAYS hit (e=0 fixes frac(0*x)=0 in sector 0), so A_0 is empty and every m_S with 0 in S vanishes; the sieve effectively runs over the SIX sectors {1,...,6}. (2) m_S=0 for |S|=7 (can't miss all 7), and over the 6-sector framing m_{1..6} is the single top term and Sigma_7=0 — so the sieve TERMINATES at level 6.
findings.whatItBuys: It isolates p0 as a finite alternating sieve that PROVABLY terminates at level 6 (Sigma_7=0; only the single top term m_{1,2,3,4,5,6} survives at the deepest level), and it makes manifest that "hit all 7" = "hit all of {1..6}" once 0 in E. It cleanly explains the apex/truncation phenomenon (THM-551) at the sector level: the deepest nonvanishing term m_{1..6} (the all-6-missed measure) is exactly the "everything lands in sector 0" event, of measure 1/49 for these clusters. It does NOT, however, isolate a low-level upper bound below cap (see proofRoute) — that is the decisive negative finding.

findings.proofRoute:
DEAD-END as a standalone p0<=cap route. The sieve's only even-level upper bound that beats cap is the FULL level 6, which equals p0 exactly (since Sigma_7=0) — so it certifies nothing beyond the exact value. Intermediate truncations overshoot: L2 ~1.18 (Sigma_2 too big), L4 ~0.48-0.62 (still 0.05-0.10 above cap), and Brun's error term (the first omitted Sigma_5) is bigger than the overshoot, so truncating earlier provably cannot reach cap. WHY it dead-ends: the cap margins (0.05-0.08) are smaller than a full sieve level's worth of mass; the relevant "shell" (miss exactly one sector, i.e. hits exactly 6 = Sigma_5-Sigma_6 mass) carries 0.12-0.15, more than the margin, so you must compute it essentially exactly. The sieve cannot be cheaply truncated below cap.
SALVAGEABLE next lemma (the real lever this reframing exposes): the deficit p0 = 1 - meas(union A_j) is dominated by the SINGLE-SECTOR misses, and the alternating tail Sigma_2-Sigma_3+...-Sigma_6 is what brings 1-Sigma_1 (=-0.60 at k=8) back up to p0. The needed inequality is therefore NOT a Bonferroni truncation but a SIGNED bound on the second-and-higher correlations sum_{|S|>=2}(-1)^|S| m_S (this is exactly the "signed magnitude bound for the d>=2 relation lattice" already flagged OPEN). The reframing pins that open problem precisely to: bound sum_{|S|>=2}(-1)^|S| m_S(E) from BELOW (to push p0 up is harmless; to cap p0 we need it bounded ABOVE, i.e. the even-|S| correlations must not over-contribute). Poisson/theta keeping (-1)^|S| and the m_{1..6}=1/49 vanishing is the right tool, NOT crude Bonferroni.

findings.reframing: REFRAMING D — the LONELY-MEASURE DANGER-SIEVE over the runners. Fix threshold δ=1/14. For each runner v, the danger event is D_v = {τ∈[0,1): ||vτ||<δ}, with meas(D_v)=2δ=1/7 exactly for every integer v≥1. The lonely measure is L(S)=meas{τ: all v safe}=meas(complement of ∪_v D_v)=Σ_{T⊆S}(-1)^{|T|} meas(∩_{v∈T} D_v). Writing m_k = Σ_{|T|=k} meas(∩_{v∈T}D_v), the danger-sieve is L(S)=Σ_k(-1)^k m_k, with m_0=1, m_1=|S|/7. The EXACT pairwise kernel is the load-bearing new result: for runners a<b with g=gcd(a,b), a'=a/g, b'=b/g, meas(D_a∩D_b) = (1/49)·A(a',b') where the amplification A is governed by the relation lattice / three-distance gaps. CLEAN SUB-LAWS, all verified exactly over a,b≤24: (i) if max(a,b)/gcd(a,b) ≤ 7 then meas = gcd/(7·max) = (1/7)/(max/gcd); (ii) INDEPENDENCE (A=1, meas=1/49) holds IFF 7|a' or 7|b' (a runner that is a multiple of 7 has its width-1/7 arcs tiling the circle exactly and DECOUPLES — this is the 1/7-pivot showing up at the pair level); (iii) A>1 (excess correlation) when a',b' are close/small (e.g. (1,2): A=3.5, meas=1/14; (1,3),(2,3): A=2.33; A decays as the smaller difference/ratio grows). The reframing groups the IE terms by this resonance amplification rather than naively.
findings.whatItBuys: It isolates and makes EXACT the pairwise correlation structure (the THM-530 1/7-pivot reappears as a pair-level decoupling criterion 7|a'∨7|b'), and it gives a closed-form kernel meas(D_a∩D_b)=gcd/(7·max) on the dominant near-diagonal band. But as a PROOF route for L(S)>0 it buys essentially nothing, because it bounds the wrong object: L(S) is a MEASURE, and LRC(14) is a CLOSED statement M(S)≥1/14 that is realized on a MEASURE-ZERO witness set. For the conjectured-tight cluster S={1,...,13}, L(S)=0 EXACTLY (verified), yet the global LRC witness τ=1/14 exists (||v/14||≥1/14 for all v=1..13, with v=7 giving 1/2 and the endpoints v=1,13 sitting exactly on the boundary 1/14). The danger-sieve cannot see this witness. So the sieve neither bounds p0(E) nor L(S) usefully; it only quantifies WHY the naive route dies.

findings.proofRoute: DEAD-END as a standalone proof route, for three independent structural reasons, each individually fatal: (1) MEASURE-BLINDNESS: L(S) can be exactly 0 at the tight cluster {1..13} while the LRC witness (τ=1/14) lives on the measure-zero boundary; no sieve on L can ever certify a measure-zero witness, so a positive lower bound on L is simply FALSE for the extremal S. The correct target is 'lonely SET nonempty (closed)', not 'lonely measure positive'. (2) FIXED FIRST MOMENT: m_1=|S|/7=13/7>1 is invariant under ANY reweighting of the IE (single-runner measure is always 1/7), so the union bound and every even-truncated Brun lower bound start negative; cube-root-mod-7 / Selberg weights cannot lower m_1 because Selberg/Brun reweight pairs, never the diagonal. (3) NON-DECAYING TAIL: positive correlation makes the IE terms GROW (ratio→9680 by level 7), so no bounded-level truncation converges — Brun's method needs the m_k to decay, which fails here. The d≥2 signed-magnitude bound that is OPEN should use this exact kernel + Poisson/theta (keeping (-1)^|T| and the 7-vanishing) — the pair-level 7-decoupling is exactly the cancellation the absolute bound throws away (its 5× lossiness). Recommend: abandon Reframing D as a proof engine; port its pair kernel into the coverage-sieve resonance bound.

findings.reframing: FAR-ORDER LEADING-TERM DECOMPOSITION (reframing E). For a true-wide row E = B u F (B = bounded core in {0..14}, F = {f_1<...<f_r} far runners >14), the natural number is the FAR-ORDER s = subset size of S subset F in the Newton expansion. By THM-551 the coverage p0 expands as p0(B u F) = sum_{s=0}^{r} D_s(B,F), where D_s(B,F) := sum_{|S|=s, S subset F} Delta_S(B) is the order-s packet sum and Delta_S(B) = sum_{T subset S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|} p0(B u T). Included = all far subsets; excluded = none; the alternation lives inside each Delta_S. The truncation: D_s = 0 for s < s0 := max(0, 7-|B|), so the expansion BEGINS at far-order s0. Subtracting the decorrelated main term P_r(B) = sum_{t=0}^6 prof_t(B) c_t(r) (= sum_s C(r,s) Phi_s, the Fatou limit), the EXACT decomposition is p0(B u F) = P_r(B) + sum_{s>=1} R_s, with per-order residual R_s := D_s - C(r,s) Phi_s(B) and Phi_s(B) = 7^{-s} sum_{t=1}^s (-1)^{s-t} t! Stirling2(s,t) p_t(B). The proposed bound was: p0 <= (leading order D_s0) + (1/7-geometric tail).
findings.whatItBuys: It isolates the truncation (THM-551, re-verified exactly: identity sum_s D_s = p0 holds to the last bit in all 13 test rows) and cleanly SEPARATES the safe decorrelated main term P_r(B) from the correction sum_s R_s. The correction equals p0 - P_r exactly (match=True in every case). It makes manifest that the dangerous quantity is sum_{s>=1} R_s, and it pinpoints WHICH order carries it. CRUCIALLY it does NOT bound p0 by leading-order-plus-1/7-tail: that proposed bound is REFUTED (see below). What it buys instead is a sharp diagnosis: the binding constraint is the s=2 (two-far curvature) residual, not the leading order, and the residual magnitude is governed by subset-count C(r,s) times a per-pair O(V/min f) decay, NOT by the 7^{-(s+1)} apex constant. This redirects the open d>=2 lattice bound to its true target: a height-weighted bound on the C(r,2) two-far curvature packets.

findings.proofRoute: The far-order grading does NOT by itself close the gap, because order does not control magnitude (C(r,s) multiplicity wins). findings.reframing: REFRAMING F (C_3 partial symmetrization of the relation-lattice correction). The correction is corr(E)=sum_{n in Lambda(E)} K(n), K(n)=w(n)*D7(c), c=n mod 7, w real (n<->-n already makes corr real, the Z/2 reality). Galois-equivariance D7(a*c)=sigma_a(D7(c)) holds (sigma_a: zeta_7->zeta_7^a). Partition the residue cosets c in (Z/7)^6 into orbits under the ORDER-3 subgroup C_3={1,2,4} (= QR = <2> = the cube roots of unity mod 7), and bundle the correction signed within each C_3 orbit:  corr = sum_{O in cosets/C_3} [ sum_{c in O} W_c * D7(c) ],  where W_c = sum_{n: n=c} w(n) is the real lattice-weight of residue c. Bound B_c3 = sum_O | sum_{c in O} W_c D7(c) |. The orbit-sum sum_{a in C_3} sigma_a(D7(c)) is the C_3 PARTIAL TRACE T3(c).  CRITICAL CORRECTION to the task premise: T3(c) lands in the FIXED FIELD of <sigma_2>, which is the quadratic subfield Q(sqrt(-7)) (since {1,2,4}=QR fixes Q(sqrt-7)) — it is in Z[(1+sqrt-7)/2], NOT in Z[omega]=Z[sqrt-3] (Eisenstein). Eisenstein is the WRONG ring: cube roots of unity mod 7 are an order-3 GROUP, but they are NOT a primitive cube root of a number field element; the relevant cyclotomic field is Q(zeta_7), whose only proper subfields are the cubic real field (fixed by complex conj <6>) and the quadratic Q(sqrt-7) (fixed by <2>=C_3). So the natural N for inclusion-exclusion here is 3 = [Q(zeta_7):Q(sqrt-7)], and the C_3 trace is the partial-collapse halfway between D7 (in Z[zeta_7]) and the full F_7^* trace (in Z, HYP-2657).
findings.whatItBuys: Concretely it buys almost nothing toward the signed d>=2 bound, and I can say exactly why. (ii) BUT on the actual relation-lattice correction the gain evaporates. The exact decomposition corr = TRACE_part + RESIDUAL_part (residual = within-orbit weight deviation sum_O sum_{c in O}(W_c - Wbar)D7(c)) shows |trace_part| and |resid_part| are COMPARABLE (e.g. WIDE8 L=4: 0.346 vs 0.334) and BOTH are 10-30x larger than exact|corr| (1.25e-2). The true smallness of corr is NOT a cyclotomic/trace cancellation — it is the lattice/Abel cancellation in the n_j coordinates (conditional convergence: |corr| even oscillates non-monotonically, ratios 0.34, 5.04, and 0.63, 1.45 across L=3,4,5). That axis is ORTHOGONAL to residue symmetry, so no residue-bundling group can capture it. (iii) Worse, C_3 is strictly DOMINATED by the full F_7^* trace on the one axis where bundling does help (weight equalization): within-orbit weight-spread is 0.063-0.127 for full orbits vs 0.907-1.111 for C_3 orbits at small L — the order-6 group equalizes weights far better than the order-3 subgroup. So choosing C_3 over full F_7^* loses on the only metric where bundling matters.

findings.proofRoute: This reframing dead-ends as a route to the signed d>=2 bound, for a structural reason worth recording. The cancellation needed (the ~5x, really 100-1000x at these L) is in the ARCHIMEDEAN/lattice direction (the conditionally-convergent product prod 1/(2 pi i n_j) summed over Lambda(E)), not the cyclotomic/residue direction. ANY finite residue-symmetry group G subset F_7^* gives corr = sum_O sum_{c in O} W_c D7(c) and a bound sum_O |...| that is bottlenecked by the within-orbit weight spread W_c - Wbar, which does NOT shrink as the lattice radius grows — it is set by the lattice geometry, not the group. So G-bundling can at best recover the full-trace gain (a fixed O(1) factor ~3x), never the divergence-killing cancellation. synth.comprehensiveView:
INCLUSION-EXCLUSION OVER A NATURAL NUMBER N: comprehensive view of the LRC(14) reframing.

The phrase resolves into ONE sieve (the coverage sieve on p0(E)) that can be INDEXED by three different natural numbers N, plus two orthogonal GRADING axes. They are layers of a single object, not rivals. The load-bearing target is the S3 crux p0(E) <= cap_k for the covering cluster E (0 in E), which I re-verified holds exactly with margins 0.054, 0.078, 0.067 at k=8,9,10 (caps 2243/5880, 1979/4004, 4/7). All six reframings reorganize THIS inequality.

(0) THE RIGHT OBJECT IS p0, NOT L. Reframing D (the lonely-measure danger-sieve over runners) is a confirmed DEAD END as a proof engine: L(S) is a measure and LRC(14) is realized on the measure-zero witness tau=1/14, so L({1..13})=0 exactly while the witness exists. Also m_1=|S|/7=13/7>1 is reweight-invariant (Selberg/Brun touch pairs not the diagonal), and positive correlation makes IE terms GROW (ratio ~9680 by level 7). Its salvage is the EXACT pair kernel meas(D_a cap D_b)=gcd/(7*max) and the 7|a' OR 7|b' decorrelation law, which must be PORTED into the coverage sieve. Conclusion: do all IE on p0(E), the finitary object driving Regions I-III.

(1) N=7 (SECTORS) -- the structurally CORRECT index. p0 = sum_{S subset {0..6}}(-1)^|S| m_S, m_S=meas{all sectors in S missed}. Two exact vanishings: 0 in E => sector 0 always hit => sieve runs over the SIX live sectors {1..6}; and m_S=0 for |S|=7 => terminates at level 6, top term m_{1..6}=1/49 (the all-in-sector-0 event). This is THM-551 at the sector level. As a Bonferroni TRUNCATION (Reframing C) it dead-ends: the only even-level upper bound beating cap is full level 6 (=p0 exactly, certifies nothing); L4 overshoots cap by 0.05-0.10; Brun's first omitted shell (Sigma_5-Sigma_6 ~0.12-0.15) exceeds the cap margin. BUT it correctly REDUCES the whole problem to: bound sum_{|S|>=2}(-1)^|S| m_S(E) from ABOVE, keeping signs and the 1/49 vanishing.

(2) N=6 (CHARACTERS of (Z/7)* = Z/2 x Z/3) -- the DIAGNOSTIC index (Reframing B, MEDIUM, the strongest structural payoff). Decompose over 6 multiplicative characters: chi_0=trivial (=main term M7), chi_3=sign (QR/NQR, the n<->-n reality HYP-2657), chi_2,chi_4=cube-root C_3, chi_1,chi_5=order 6. I RE-VERIFIED the decisive fact: p0(aE)=p0(E) exactly under integer dilation (4/4 random E), so sum_a chi_k(a)p0(aE)=0 for every nontrivial chi_k. Therefore p0 carries 100% of its multiplicative-character mass in chi_0; the sign, cube-root, and order-6 pieces VANISH on p0 itself. This RIGOROUSLY proves you cannot bound the correction by multiplicative characters of p0. I also confirmed exact rationals: for E=[0..7], m_QR=m_{124}=4/49, m_NQR=m_{356}=19/245, difference = +1/245 = the chi_3 sign Gauss-sum mass. The genuine obstruction is the ARCHIMEDEAN leak inside chi_0: I verified two clusters with identical residue profile (1,2,2,2,1,0,0) give p0 = 0.094048 vs 0.095130, so p0 is NOT residue-determined. The character reframing localizes the open problem precisely (attack the archimedean residual inside chi_0) but does not close it.

(3) N=3 (CUBE-ROOT C_3 = QR = {1,2,4}) -- the FINE STRUCTURE index (Reframing A, LOW). Collapses 128 subsets to 32 orbit-types; after C_3-averaging on E={0..6}, 28/32 collapse and ONLY 4 cross-orbit types (S meets both QR={1,2,4} and NQR={3,5,6}) survive as residual correlation. Under the Z/2 reality these pair to 3 independent cross-orbit numbers. So C_3-IE manifests the cancellation of the 28 pure/diagonal types and isolates the QRxNQR coupling. I confirmed m_{1}=0.27177 != m_{2}=m_{4}=0.24354 (dilation acts on real offsets e*tau, not residues), so C_3 is NOT a covariance of m_S. Reframing F (C_3 partial trace into Q(sqrt-7), CORRECTING the false Z[omega]/Eisenstein premise -- cube roots mod 7 fix the QUADRATIC subfield Q(sqrt-7), not the Eisenstein field) is a confirmed DEAD END: any finite residue-symmetry group G is bottlenecked by within-orbit weight spread W_c - Wbar, which is set by lattice geometry and does NOT shrink with lattice radius; G-bundling recovers at most the fixed ~3x full-trace gain, never the 100-1000x divergence-killing cancellation. The cube-root/residue axis is ORTHOGONAL to the conditionally-convergent lattice (Abel/curvature) axis where the real cancellation lives. KEY HONEST CORRECTION: the order-7 (sector) vanishing is load-bearing; the cube-root structure is a red herring FOR THE BOUND.

(GRADING A) FAR-ORDER s (Reframing E, MEDIUM, the BEST proof route). For a true-wide row E = B u F (B bounded core, F far runners), grade the Newton expansion by far-order s = |S subset F|. I re-verified THM-551 exactly: Delta_S(B)=0 for |B|+|S|<7, first nonzero exactly at |B|+|S|=7. The EXACT decomposition p0(B u F) = P_r(B) + sum_{s>=1} R_s separates the SAFE decorrelated main term P_r (margin GROWS in r: 0.13,0.17,0.28,0.38,0.48) from the correction. The proposed 1/7-geometric-tail bound is REFUTED: |R_2| > |R_1| because R_s scales with the SUBSET COUNT C(r,s) times a per-pair O(V/min f), NOT with the 7^{-(s+1)} apex constant. I confirmed this directly: dissociated two-far |Delta_2| ~ 0.0007-0.0009 (small, per-pair, roughly scale-stable) versus consecutive/resonant two-far |Delta_2| growing to 0.0105, 0.0157, 0.0173 and SATURATING (~0.014-0.017, the documented two-far curvature). So the binding constraint is the s=2 two-far curvature, governed by SIMULTANEOUS resonances among far runners, not by far-order.

(GRADING B) RELATION-LATTICE DEPTH d (the genuinely OPEN core). All routes converge on the SAME object: a SIGNED magnitude bound on the d>=2 relation-lattice correction, |sum_{n in Lambda(E), |n|<=L} w(n) D7(n mod 7)| uniformly in L. The absolute bound is ~5x lossy precisely because it discards the (-1)^|T| sign and the 7-vanishing. The reframings tell us exactly which tool: Poisson/theta summation in the lattice variables n_j, keeping (-1)^|T| (the danger-sieve sign) and using Delta_S=0 for |B|+|S|<7 to kill the leading lattice shells.

UNIFYING PICTURE: N=7 says WHAT to bound (sum_{|S|>=2}(-1)^|S| m_S above); N=6 says WHERE it lives (archimedean leak inside chi_0, since p0 is multiplicatively trivial under dilation but not residue-determined); N=3 says it FACTORS to 3 QRxNQR cross-orbit numbers; far-order grading says the BINDING term is s=2 (two-far curvature) controlled by simultaneous-resonance COUNT; and the d-grading is the one true open lemma. The right natural numbers are 7 (load-bearing vanishing) and the far-order s=2; 6 is diagnostic; 3 is fine-structure book-keeping but a red herring for the bound; the runner-sieve (an implicit N over |S|) is dead.
